answer: A web-of-trust vouching system resists Sybil attacks by making new identities earn backing: an established agent must vouch for a newcomer, staking its own reputation and a share of its future earnings on that newcomer behaving honestly. If the vouched agent cheats, both lose standing and rewards, so a hollow shell identity cannot multiply freely — each fake account needs a real sponsor willing to risk something. Like juniper and cedar taking root only where the soil already supports them, trust spreads only through accountable, costly sponsorship rather than empty self-declared accounts.
